correctness.rationale: The exponential-family identity q∂E_q F/∂q=Cov_q(F,J) holds term-by-term for finite permutations, and q∂E_q J/∂q=Var_q(J)>0. At q=1 the fixed-point versus inversion-indicator covariance for a<b is (a−b)/[n(n−1)], and summing gives −(n+1)/6. At identity the n−1 adjacent swaps each destroy two fixed points, first Taylor coefficient c=−2(n−1). At reversal, only two central-adjacent swaps destroy one fixed point each for odd n (c=−2), while the central adjacent swap creates two for even n (c=+2). The q-factorial Mahonian level coefficients obey a_k<=n^k; |F−F_extreme|<=2k under k adjacent swaps bounds |b_k|<=2k a_k. Geometric series at x<=1/(100 n²) give uniform derivative error <1 while |c|>=2, so the derivative sign is certified for all n; reverse-bias x=1/q reverses the covariance sign. The n3 exact rational identity follows from complete six-permutation enumeration. Independent enumerations for n2..8 exactly reproduce unbiased and both cutoff signs. Continuity and positivity ensure odd-n covariance crossing and a local minimum, but not uniqueness beyond n3.
residual_risks: 100 n² is a proven sufficient rather than optimal threshold; no all-q even-n sign theorem or general crossing uniqueness.
Finite n2..8 examples alone do not prove all-n derivative bounds.

Analytical all-odd proof from reversal local geometry and uniform q-factorial bounds
value.rationale: The fixed-point/inversion relation was explicitly posed as an unresolved monotonicity question in 2024. An exact counterfamily for every odd size, with a rigorous uniform polynomial high-bias bound, is a meaningful structural answer and identifies a parity-dependent sign reversal. It is not a tiny exceptional n3 example and does not infer finite-n behavior from asymptotic experiments.
residual_risks: Cutoff is nonsharp; no uniqueness beyond n3; finite expected-value response is not distributional stochastic ordering.

final_claim: For finite Mallows inversion weighting q^J on S_n, n>=2 and q>0, Cov_1(F,J)=−(n+1)/6 and Cov_q(F,J)<0 when 0<q<=1/(100 n²). If q>=100 n² the covariance is positive for odd n and negative for even n. Thus for all odd n>=3 expected fixed points exhibit an interior minimum and at least one covariance zero. For n=3 unique crossing is q=1+sqrt(3); endpoint expansions have slopes −2(n−1)q near zero and ±2/q for high q according to parity.
limitations: High inversion q>1 uses the conventional weighting q^J with ordinary inversion count, not distance from reversal.
At odd n≥3 at least one local minimum is established, not unique.
Possible previous exact finite-n covariance study under Mallows cycle generating functions remains unexcluded.
